items.title: Roland Hanna interviewed by Monk Rowe, Scottsdale, Arizona, April 15, 2000
items.q: Anton Rubenstein was a great improviser.

ctx.x: Isn’t it curious that a lot of classical musicians are enamored sometimes of what a jazz player can do. At the same time a jazz musician looks at what they do.

Well you know it always seemed to me that the guys who really are the giants are the composers who recognize how important it is to improvise. Rachmaninoff was a great improviser. Anton Rubenstein was a great improviser. Bussoni, Tosic, they were great improvisers. They could sit down and improvise on a Bach fugue. And anybody who plays the fugues, they know what I’m talking about. They know how difficult it is to do that. But they were also people who analyzed constantly. They were never people who just played…
So when you play Mozart or Beethoven, you’re most likely recognizing the harmonies as they go by.
